How to read the numbers and the quantum part

Distance

d = √(Δx² + Δy² + Δz²). Coordinates and distance use fictional space units (su), not AU or light-years. Planets are fixed; no gravity, orbits, or travel times are modeled.

Clustering score

0.15 × squared group sizes + normalized distances between same-group planets. Lower means tighter, more balanced groups. This is a surrogate score, not a travel distance.

Shots and valid tours

One shot is one final bitstring measurement. A valid tour visits each assigned planet once and returns to the station. Invalid measurements are counted, not secretly repaired.

What is quantum here?

The CPU emulates a quantum atom register to propose assignments and route-edge choices. Three-planet tours are labeled classical/trivial. The planet coordinates are 3D; the physical atom layout is a separate 2D register.
